components.name: Chip
components.description: A status pill. The tone class swaps hue, text, border and a 16% fill together — colour never travels alone.

components.name: Seg Bar
components.description: The core idiom. One hue per bar; the reading is carried by the phosphor ramp alone — dim .10, second .30, lit .62, head .85.

components.name: Panel
components.description: A flat deck face. Depth is one inset sheen and a 2px lift on a fine pointer — never an ambient shadow.

narrative.overview: Steward is an instrument-dark flight deck for one machine: a lit dial for the number that matters, segmented LED bars for every other quantity, a phosphor scope for the trace over time, and a small character docked in the corner who reports and refuses. Nothing lit is decorative — every lit thing is a reading. A day shift lights the same deck from outside rather than replacing it.
keyCharacteristics: One dial, many segmented bars — quantity has exactly one visual idiom
Machine data is always mono and always tabular
A lit thing means a measurement, not an alarm
Character in the form; literalism in the facts
Observation only — the strongest gesture files something for review
Reduced motion is gentler, never blank

rules.name: The Hue Law
rules.body: A lit arc or bar never changes hue or opacity with its value. Status colour lives on the chip beside the instrument, never in the stroke. Amber belongs to band markers and status chips; coral appears only at 99.5% used or higher, at the 90 marker, on risk-high, or when a reading did not come back.

rules.name: The 8 Degree Floor
rules.body: Any nonzero dial value draws at least 8 degrees on the 240 degree sweep (12 on the ring). Low is a confident short stroke, never a faint one; a true zero draws nothing.

rules.name: The Seg Idiom
rules.body: Every quantity that is not the dial is a segmented LED bar on the ramp 0.10 / 0.30 / 0.62 / 0.85, head cell hot, at most 48 cells, two tones maximum.

rules.name: The One-Motion Rule
rules.body: One data-state drives exactly one body animation, so swapping state cancels the previous one outright. Real activity cancels the idle antic instantly, mid-animation.

rules.name: The Scan-Bar Truth Rule
rules.body: The scan bar and the scope sweep run only during real work. Neither may imply activity that is not happening.

rules.name: The Observe-Only Seal
rules.body: Deletion never happens. A scheduled observation cannot delete, move, or upload a file; holding something for review is the strongest gesture in the product.

rules.name: The Calm Status Rule
rules.body: Red is not a mood. Growth, review, and uncertainty use ink and amber; coral means full or unreadable, and nothing else.

rules.name: Evidence Before Voice
rules.body: No character line may assert a cause, folder, or measurement the collector did not record. Only safe, low, and rebuildable count as reclaimable.

dos: Do use one segmented-bar idiom for every quantity that is not the dial.
Do keep every measured value mono and tabular.
Do show measured, inferred, unavailable, and too-early-to-call states explicitly.
Do let the character be playful about its own posture and literal about the data.
Do name the limit of each channel in its own header.
donts: Don't use alarming red system monitors, alarm theater, or manufactured urgency.
Don't ship one-click deletion, hidden risk, or a gesture stronger than hold-for-review.
Don't show opaque health scores or unsupported predictions.
Don't let the character assert a cause, folder, or measurement the collector did not record.
Don't dim, recolour, or fade an instrument to express a low value.
Don't run the scan bar or the scope sweep when no work is happening.
